question: Of the role-less officer rows, how many are classifiable at all?
would_any_row_become_CEO_or_PRESIDENT: NO -- MAPPABLE contains no CEO or PRESIDENT target, deliberately. Promoting a divisional title into CEO is the bug that made officer_features.ceo_of() return FedEx Dataworks' CEO for FDX.
why_this_changes_nothing_yet: officers.json feeds officer_features.py, which fills trained NEO features (NEO_COUNT, NEO_TURNOVER, CEO_DUALITY, CEO_TENURE) in the equities MTNN. Relabelling rows moves a model input. This script produces the number that decides whether that is worth doing; it does not do it.

unclassified_tail_shape.reading: A long tail of idiosyncratic abbreviations -- 'CVP, Critical Care', 'Chf Rsch, Dev & Innov Officer', 'Sr MD Gl Hd Commodity & Option' -- not a missing rule. A handful are mappable with more patterns ('CVP PRIN ACCT OFFICER' -> CAO, 'E.V.P. Finance & C.F.O.' -> CFO, 'Senior Executive VicePresident' -> EVP), worth perhaps another 50 rows. Each new pattern after that buys single-digit row counts.

verdict: DO NOT RELABEL. The best case is roughly 250 of 56,257 rows (0.44%) across 27 tickers, and it costs moving a trained model input: officers.json feeds officer_features.py, which fills NEO_COUNT / NEO_TURNOVER / CEO_DUALITY / CEO_TENURE in the equities MTNN. The nearest measured floor is the officer-features A/B, where arm A's sector_acc seed RANGE over 3 seeds was 0.0209 and the between-arm delta of 0.0132 did not clear it (ab_officer_features.json). A 0.44% change in one feature's inputs is not measurable against that and would force a re-run of the shipped model to find out. The 828 DIVISIONAL rows are the genuinely interesting population and they should stay role-less -- promoting a subsidiary title into CEO or PRESIDENT is the bug that made officer_features.ceo_of() return FedEx Dataworks' CEO for FDX.
headline: 3017 role-less rows is NOT 3017 classifier misses. 1111 (36.8%) carry no title at all -- the filer wrote 'See Remarks' or similar and the title lives in a free-text block the parser never sees. 201 are real titles the classifier does not recognise. The rest are divisional or genuinely unclassified.
CORRECTION_0209_was_misattributed: An earlier version of this verdict said 'the equities seed spread on SECTOR ACCURACY was 0.0209'. 0.0209 is from ab_officer_features.json -- a different experiment -- and it is a RANGE over 3 seeds, not an sd. The sector-LABELS A/B (ab_sector_labels.json, 5 seeds) has arm sd 0.0098 and arm range 0.0252. Quoting one experiment's number as another's, and a range where sds were being compared, is the same defect this phase keeps finding, in my own writeup.
